q: An equity-oriented mutual fund must invest at least what proportion in domestic equity?
e: An equity-oriented scheme must hold at least 65% in domestic equities to be classified as equity-oriented for tax purposes. Below this threshold, the scheme is taxed as a non-equity (debt-like) fund.

q: For an equity-oriented mutual fund, Long Term Capital Gains (held > 12 months) are taxed at (post-July 2024 rules):
e: Post-July 2024: Equity LTCG (> 12 months) = 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh per FY. Pre-July 2024 rates were 10% above ₹1 lakh.

q: Equity-oriented MF Short Term Capital Gains (held ≤ 12 months) are taxed at (post-July 2024):
e: Post-July 2024: Equity STCG = 20% flat (changed from 15%). Pre-July 2024 rates were 15%.

q: Debt mutual funds bought on or after April 1, 2023 are taxed at:
o: Slab rate, regardless of holding period (no indexation, no LTCG benefit)
e: Debt funds bought on or after April 1, 2023 are taxed at investor's slab rate, regardless of holding period. No indexation, no LTCG concession. Old debt holdings (pre-April 2023) follow the older 36-month / 20%-with-indexation rule.

q: ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Scheme) has a mandatory lock-in period of:
e: ELSS has a 3-year lock-in — the shortest among Section 80C tax-saving instruments (PPF: 15 years, FD: 5 years). Eligible for ₹1.5 lakh deduction under Section 80C.
